issues.legal_issue: A pre-constitutional law placed in the protected constitutional schedule is immune from a challenge based on the property guarantee carried over from the former constitutional order.
material_facts: The challenged acquisition law was enacted before the Constitution and was later placed in the protected constitutional schedule.
The challenge alleged that the law’s compensation provisions violated the property protection in the former constitutional order.
The appellants argued that the law was void when enacted and therefore could not receive constitutional protection.
issues.conclusion: The law and its challenged provisions were protected from the challenge. The fact that the law predated the Constitution, or was alleged to have violated the former property guarantee, did not prevent that protection from applying.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31B protects laws placed in the Ninth Schedule against challenges based on rights in Part III, including where the asserted right derives from Section 299(2) of the Government of India Act, 1935, which was carried into Article 31(2). Article 366(10) did not exclude the pre-constitutional law from that protection. The Court applied Dhirubha Devisingh Gohil v. State of Bombay and State of Uttar Pradesh v. H.H. Maharaja Brijendra Singh. It distinguished N.B. Jeejeebhoy v. Assistant Collector because the law there did not have Ninth Schedule protection.

rule.if: constitutional_validity_appeal and preconstitutional_law and law_in_protected_schedule and challenge_based_on_former_property_guarantee

predicates.constitutional_validity_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the constitutional validity of a law or its provisions.
predicates.preconstitutional_law: The challenged law was enacted before the Constitution came into force.
predicates.law_in_protected_schedule: The challenged law was placed in a constitutional schedule that protects listed laws from specified rights-based challenges.
predicates.challenge_based_on_former_property_guara: The challenge relies on a property guarantee from the former constitutional order that was carried into the later Constitution.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a pre-constitutional law placed in the protected schedule on the basis of the former property guarantee, the challenge is barred by constitutional protection.

issues.legal_issue: A court may not examine whether compensation principles are relevant or whether the resulting compensation is illusory when the challenged provisions are protected from the property-rights challenge.
material_facts: The appellants argued that the compensation formula produced illusory compensation by limiting the relevant market value to an earlier valuation benchmark with an addition.
The challenged provisions were part of a law placed in the protected constitutional schedule.
The appeals sought to invalidate those provisions on the basis of the property guarantee in the former constitutional order.
issues.conclusion: The Court could not examine whether the prescribed valuation principles were relevant or whether the compensation was illusory, because the provisions were protected from the asserted property-rights challenge.
issues.legal_principle: Article 31B and the Ninth Schedule foreclosed examination of a challenge based on the property guarantee in repealed Article 31 where the challenged provisions enjoyed that protection. The Court treated Rustom Cavasjee Cooper v. Union of India and State of Gujarat v. Shantilal Mangaldas as irrelevant to that threshold bar, and agreed with the High Court’s conclusion upholding the provisions.

predicates.compensation_validity_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal challenging the validity of provisions that determine compensation for acquired property.
predicates.protected_compensation_provisions: The challenged compensation provisions are part of a law protected from the asserted rights-based challenge.
predicates.challenge_claims_illusory_compensation: The challenger alleges that the compensation formula produces illusory compensation or uses irrelevant valuation principles.

issues.definition: If an appeal challenges protected compensation provisions by claiming illusory compensation, the court cannot review the compensation principles on that basis.
